focus.jnote: The macro tail is a one-two punch: Wednesday’s hot CPI and today’s 8:30 ET data cluster. US September CPI released on Wednesday rose 3.7% year-over-year, higher than the market expectation of 3.6%, raising concerns over further rate hikes. Overnight the AI trade cracked harder — global equities fell as a selloff in the artificial-intelligence trade gathered speed and pushed investors toward bonds; S&P 500 futures were down 0.3% while Nasdaq 100 contracts retreated 1.3%. Asia was ugly: the Economic Times reported a nearly 5% drop in Tokyo, and Moneycontrol reported nearly 8% in Seoul. At 8:30 ET, September PPI is forecast to rise 0.5% month over month while retail sales are expected to increase 0.3%, and initial jobless claims are forecast at 195,000 with the Philadelphia Fed index expected at 26.5. Fed Chair Warsh speaks at ~11:30 ET. Yields actually eased in the flight to safety (the benchmark 10-year US Treasury yield falls around 7 basis points to 5.08%, its lowest level in three weeks). The scanner boarded four names into this — validate all hard at 9:35.
focus.notdown: Two bullish Type C breakouts boarded — GME and TBBB — but both are multi-day-old breakouts fading into a risk-off open. GameStop stock hit a 52-week high as CEO Cohen bought $23M in shares, but it closed Wednesday down and is trading at $26.31 in the after-hours session, down 3.09% from the regular market close of $27.15 — below its $26.53 pivot, a failing-breakout risk. TBBB set a fresh high this week (a new 52-week high of $55.91) but trades well extended above its pivot. On a risk-off, post-hot-CPI tape, breakouts are the exact setup that fails — both are watch-only.
focus.notup: Two bearish Type A gaps boarded — MAN and FHN — and both share the same fatal flaw: near-zero confirming volume, plus catalysts that cut the wrong way. ManpowerGroup’s results matched Wall Street expectations — adjusted EPS of $1.01 matched the Zacks estimate, and First Horizon reported Q3 non-GAAP EPS of $0.53, slightly beating consensus by $0.01. Both are in-line-to-beat prints with soft revenue, not clean guidance-cut misses — shorting either on sub-0.1x relative volume into an 8:30 data cluster is exactly the blow-up 4-VAL exists to prevent. On a RED day, sell nothing new unless it’s hard-validated at reduced size.
focus.why: Why RED? Two independent locks: a scheduled 8:30 ET data cluster (PPI, retail sales, jobless claims inside 24h — the master rules forbid GREEN and default to stand-down/roll-DTE), and P(≥1% gap) at ~42% is above the 35% trigger with composite ~56 in WARM. Layer on a fourth-day AI/chip rout that gapped Asia 5–8% overnight, a still-hot 3.7% CPI behind us, and a VIX that popped ~10% Wednesday toward 17, and this is an open-ended, two-sided tape. The four boarded names are all compromised — the two bears gapped on near-zero volume off in-line prints, and the two breakouts are days-old and fading. Stand down on new credit spreads, or push DTE past the data and cut size hard. Cash is a position today.

setups.read: ManpowerGroup (MAN) is a bearish Type A boarded at Grade A+ — the scanner’s top-graded name — but read the caution here, don’t take it blind. The print was essentially in line, not a clean miss: the company posted profit of 71 cents a share, adjusted earnings of $1.01, and the results matched Wall Street expectations — the average estimate was also for $1.01. The gap is a revenue miss (revenue of $4.84 billion missed the $4.91 billion the four analysts surveyed by Zacks expected). Four honest cautions: (1) the scanner shows relative volume ~0.09x — far below the 1.3x confirmation bar, the single biggest red flag; (2) the scanner’s prior close ($51.96) implies a ~17.5% gap-down, but the options-implied move was only ~7.8% — a huge overshoot that can mean-revert hard; (3) the scanner flags NO S/R layers within 12% — nothing between the stock and a short strike; (4) no OI data returned. ATM spread $0.10 passes. Next earnings ~Jan 2027, outside DTE. On a RED, data-cluster day this is strictly 4-VAL-at-9:35, minimum size, lean skip.

setups.read: GameStop (GME) is a bullish Type C ATH breakout boarded at Grade A+ — but it’s fading into the open, which is the honest concern to flag. The breakout has held 3 sessions above the $26.53 pivot with breakout-day volume ~1.83x the 50-day average, and the insider story is strong: GameStop hit a 52-week high as CEO Cohen bought $23M in shares. The problem: GME closed Wednesday down (27.15, −0.26%) and sold off after hours — trading at $26.31 in the after-hours session, down 3.09% from the regular market close of $27.15 — which is below the $26.53 pivot. On a risk-off morning that is a potential failing breakout. On the plus side it has 3 S/R layers within 12% (pivot $26.53, sma20 $24.70, swing $24.04), OI 17,915 and a $0.10 ATM spread both pass, and next earnings ~Dec 8 is outside a 7-DTE. 4-VAL-at-9:35 only — this is a bull put, so the stock must hold ABOVE the pivot and the prior close.

setups.read: First Horizon (FHN) is a bearish Type A boarded at Grade A+ — but, like MAN, the adjusted print was a beat, which makes this counter-intuitive. FHN reported Q3 non-GAAP EPS of $0.53, slightly beating consensus by $0.01, while revenue of $883 million fell short of the $889.37 million consensus. The headline GAAP number is ugly — a net loss available to common shareholders of $(94) million, or loss per share of $(0.20) — but that is driven by one-off strategic balance-sheet actions, not core weakness: the company entered into an agreement to sell ~$4.5 billion of select lower-yielding consumer mortgages, a transaction accretive to earnings going forward. Honest cautions: (1) relative volume ~0.00x — extraordinarily thin, nowhere near 1.3x; (2) the adjusted quarter actually beat, so shorting bets the de-rate continues; (3) only 1 S/R layer within 7% (gap floor $22.67). No OI data; ATM spread $0.10 passes. Next earnings ~Jan 2027, outside DTE. On a RED data-cluster day, 4-VAL-at-9:35 only — minimum size, lean skip.
